facts.raw_span: A 13-year-old boy with T-cell lymphoblastic leukemia
receiving maintenance therapy (daily 6-mercaptopurine, weekly methotrexate, monthly vincristine and dexamethasone)
3 months of hematochezia
two to three loose bowel movements per day (Bristol type 5–6) with mixed blood
polyethylene glycol produced looser stools without reducing bleeding
denied abdominal pain, weight loss, rashes, arthritis, oral or perianal lesions
intermittently neutropenic and consistently lymphopenic
abdomen was soft and nontender
a small nonbleeding external hemorrhoid was noted
Stool studies, including culture and PCR for Clostridioides difficile, cytomegalovirus, and adenovirus, were negative
Colonoscopy showed multiple semisessile, nonbleeding 1–5 mm polyps in the rectum and sigmoid colon with surrounding erythematous, eroded mucosa
histiocytes contained numerous basophilic spherical and targetoid inclusions that were strongly positive on von Kossa and periodic acid–Schiff stains
A 13-year-old boy with T-cell lymphoblastic leukemia
receiving maintenance therapy (daily 6-mercaptopurine, weekly methotrexate, monthly vincristine and dexamethasone)
3 months of hematochezia
two to three loose bowel movements per day (Bristol type 5–6) with mixed blood
polyethylene glycol produced looser stools without reducing bleeding
denied abdominal pain, weight loss, rashes, arthritis, oral or perianal lesions
intermittently neutropenic and consistently lymphopenic
abdomen was soft and nontender
a small nonbleeding external hemorrhoid was noted
Stool studies, including culture and PCR for Clostridioides difficile, cytomegalovirus, and adenovirus, were negative
Colonoscopy showed multiple semisessile, nonbleeding 1–5 mm polyps in the rectum and sigmoid colon with surrounding erythematous, eroded mucosa
histiocytes contained numerous basophilic spherical and targetoid inclusions that were strongly positive on von Kossa and periodic acid–Schiff stains

concepts.why: The presence of basophilic spherical and targetoid inclusions in histiocytes that are positive on von Kossa and periodic acid-Schiff stains, along with the clinical presentation of hematochezia and loose bowel movements, is consistent with Whipple disease.

The patient's history of T-cell lymphoblastic leukemia and immunosuppressive therapy, combined with the symptoms of hematochezia and loose bowel movements, raises the possibility of graft-versus-host disease.

Although stool studies for cytomegalovirus were negative, the patient's immunocompromised state and symptoms of hematochezia and loose bowel movements make CMV colitis a consideration, particularly given the finding of eroded mucosa and inflammatory infiltrate on colonoscopy.
The patient's intermittent neutropenia and symptoms of hematochezia and loose bowel movements, in the context of chemotherapy, suggest the possibility of neutropenic colitis.

The patient's chemotherapy regimen, including 6-mercaptopurine and methotrexate, is associated with an increased risk of colitis, and the symptoms of hematochezia and loose bowel movements are consistent with this diagnosis.
It explains the presence of hematochezia in a patient with T-cell lymphoblastic leukemia.
It explains the negative stool studies and presence of mixed inflammatory infiltrate in a patient receiving chemotherapy.

rationales.F01: T-cell lymphoblastic leukemia may increase the risk of certain gastrointestinal complications, including malignancy-associated hemorrhagic coloproctitis.
rationales.F02: Chemotherapy can cause gastrointestinal side effects, including neutropenic colitis and chemotherapy-induced colitis.
rationales.F03: Hematochezia can be a symptom of various gastrointestinal conditions, including cytomegalovirus colitis and malignancy-associated hemorrhagic coloproctitis.
rationales.F07: Neutropenia can increase the risk of certain infections and gastrointestinal complications, including neutropenic colitis.
rationales.F10: Negative stool studies for Clostridioides difficile, cytomegalovirus, and adenovirus help rule out these infections as the cause of the patient's symptoms.
rationales.F12: The presence of basophilic spherical and targetoid inclusions in histiocytes that are positive on von Kossa and periodic acid-Schiff stains is characteristic of Whipple disease.

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient's condition, including hematochezia and loose bowel movements, in the context of T-cell lymphoblastic leukemia and its treatment, is most specifically explained by malignancy-associated hemorrhagic coloproctitis, given the direct association with the patient's malignancy and its treatment.
